newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Gujral vows to deepen economic reforms.
newsitem.headline: India's Gujral vows to deepen economic reforms.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral said on Monday his government would pursue the same policy framework as its predecessor and widen the scope of economic reforms.

"Even though there has been a change of government, there will be no change in policy framework the United Front government followed the last 10 months," said Gujral in his maiden speech after being sworn in as the prime minister earlier on Monday.
"We intend to widen the ambit of economic reform and to complete structural adjustment," Gujral told a business meeting organised by the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII).
Gujral said the nation could continue to achieve seven percent annual growth of gross domestic product (GDP), which was the average rate over the past three years.
"The seven percent target is feasible, possible and also desirable," he said.
Gujral assured the business leaders that his centre-left government would maintain continuity in economic policies.
"I commit here that economic policy continuity will be firmly assured by my government," he said.
"India can look forward to the continuation of reform and programmes, and its deepening and widening."
The government will focus on improving the nation's creaking infrastructure, dismantling administrative barriers and wooing foreign investment, Gujral said.
Inflows of foreign direct investment provided a much needed shift towards equity and away from debt, he said.
